AUDIT OF THE 2026-08-26 SESSION — FULL REPORT
====================================================================================================

19 findings survived adversarial verification (each re-run independently by a
second agent instructed to refute it). 2 block the A/B test.

PART 1 — ALL VERIFIED FINDINGS
====================================================================================================

[ 1] loss-math   VERDICT: CONFIRMED
      CLAIM: Session claim: "the structural minimum collar half-width is 2*tolerance, because the
      prediction max-pool spreads a correct peak up to 2*tolerance frames."
      CORRECTION: Claim stands as stated. Precise form: the reach of a peak at annotation+off is
      [A+off-3, A+off+3]; the union over |off|<=3 is [A-6, A+6].

[ 2] loss-math   VERDICT: CONFIRMED
      CLAIM: TempoRelativeCollarBCELoss docstring: the collar is a pure tempo-normalisation of the
      stock 'don't care' region; nothing about correct peaks being penalised. Code default
      min_half=2.
      CORRECTION: With the shipped default min_half=2, TempoRelativeCollarBCELoss actively pushes
      DOWN a correctly-placed, confident peak for all tempi above ~76 bpm — the majority of any real
      corpus. min_half must be >= 2*tolerance (6 at tolerance=3) for the loss to be sound; at
      min_half=6 it is provably clean at every tempo and peak logit tested.

[ 3] loss-math   VERDICT: REFUTED
      CLAIM: TempoRelativeCollarBCELoss docstring: "k = 0.30 leaves 70 bpm unchanged (13 frames),
      widens 40 bpm to ~22, narrows 180 bpm to ~5."
      CORRECTION: It is k=0.14 (the shipped default) that leaves 70 bpm unchanged at 13 frames
      total. The docstring's worked example describes a configuration the code does not use, and
      mislabels half-widths as frame counts.

[ 4] loss-math   VERDICT: REFUTED
      CLAIM: PhaseWeightedShiftTolerantBCELoss docstring: "sigma = 0.06 puts the half-height at
      +/-0.12 of an IBI".
      CORRECTION: sigma=0.06 puts the half-height at +/-0.0706 IBI. The docstring overstates the
      width of the subdivision bump by ~1.7x.

[ 5] corpus-data   VERDICT: CONFIRMED
      CLAIM: 'Training set: 4796' in logs vs 2349 items — reconcile

[ 6] corpus-data   VERDICT: CONFIRMED
      CLAIM: pos_weight at launch is {'beat': 32, 'downbeat': 112}; a hand calc suggested 30

[ 7] corpus-data   VERDICT: CONFIRMED
      CLAIM: Zero fold-0 leakage: no canonical SMC fold-0 stem appears in a training fold

[ 8] corpus-data   VERDICT: CONFIRMED
      CLAIM: The dataloader previously SKIPPED one-column tracks entirely rather than mis-
      supervising them

[ 9] comparability   VERDICT: CONFIRMED
      CLAIM: collar14 vs ph13 is confounded because collar14 has no phase term
      CORRECTION: collar14 vs ph13 differs in TWO variables: relative collar (k*IBI vs fixed ±6
      frames) AND presence of the phase term. The −0.014 cannot be attributed to the collar.
      Additional minor caveat: loss.py was last modified 19:00 on 08-26 and collar14's first ckpt is
      19:08 (started ~19:02), so collar14 is the only phase5 arm on the post-19:00 loss.py; whether
      that edit touched the shared ShiftTolerantBCELoss base is UNVERIFIED (no intermediate versions
      on disk, file is uncommitted).

[10] comparability   VERDICT: REFUTED
      CLAIM: all arms ran with pos_weight 32, identical
      CORRECTION: True for every OUR-arm except pw14 (beat=14, by design). It is false for the
      released reference: 20/86, not 32/112. Any of our arms compared to the released number carries
      a pos_weight difference on top of everything else.

[11] comparability   VERDICT: CONFIRMED
      CLAIM: ph13 0.6568 vs released 0.6510 confounds loss with corpus
      CORRECTION: The comparison differs in at least FOUR variables: loss (phase vs stock),
      pos_weight (32/112 vs 20/86), corpus composition, and training code. KNOWN from the
      checkpoint: the released model's loss, pos_weights, and augmentation config. NOT KNOWN from
      any artifact on this machine: the released model's exact training track list — the release
      stores no dataset manifest, so 'different corpus' rests on the published dataset list, not on
      measurement. It is ASSUMED, not verified, that it saw the same tracks as our 2678. Also note
      the release's tempo range (-20..+20) matches our default arms, so tempo augmentation is NOT
      one of the confounds.

[12] comparability   VERDICT: CONFIRMED
      CLAIM: the f0_wide stock trio is on the broken corpus so cannot baseline ph13
      CORRECTION: Confirmed. All six phase3 arms (f0_shipped_s0-s2, f0_wide_s0-s2) and both phase4
      peritem arms trained on 1954 tracks with zero SMC; ph13 trained on 2678 with 200 SMC. Note the
      phase3 pair itself is still internally valid: f0_shipped vs f0_wide differ only in tempo_min
      (-20 vs -60), same data_dir, same seed pairing (cache/run_phase3.sh). It is the cross-phase
      use of them as a ph13 baseline that is invalid.

[13] statistics   VERDICT: PARTIAL
      CLAIM: "run-to-run noise floor is ~0.007 F" — used throughout the session as the threshold
      below which differences are ignored.
      CORRECTION: A single paired difference is not a legitimate noise estimate. Defensible figure
      for a single-seed single-checkpoint fold-0 F: seed sd 0.028 (3 seeds, df=2; 95% CI [0.015,
      0.176]) combined with checkpoint sd ~0.013 gives sd ~0.031. For a two-arm comparison run at
      one seed each, the sd of the difference is sqrt(2)*0.031 = 0.044 and n=1 pair, so NO single-
      seed arm comparison on fold 0 is significant. 0.007 understates the real floor by roughly 4-6x
      and should be described as a lower bound covering GPU nondeterminism only. Every
      "outside/inside the 0.007 noise floor" judgement in the session was made against the wrong
      number.

[14] statistics   VERDICT: CONFIRMED
      CLAIM: "fold 0 is easier than the 8-fold average: released scores 0.6510 on fold 0 vs 0.6270
      over 217 tracks"
      CORRECTION: The +0.0240 gap is real as a fact about those 27 tracks, but it is NOT evidence
      that fold 0 is intrinsically easy: Welch t=0.52, p=0.605 vs the other 190 tracks, and the
      standard error of any 27-track fold mean is 0.0446, which is larger than the observed between-
      fold sd of 0.0320 — i.e. the fold-to-fold variation is essentially all sampling noise. The
      correct implication is stronger than "fold 0 is easy": any fold-0-only number carries ~0.045
      of standard error relative to the corpus value, so a fold-0 gain of 0.01-0.03 (the size the
      session was chasing) is uninformative about the 8-fold result. This applies to every fold-0
      claim in the session, including all the ph13/gph13/sig10/bidir03/collar14/peritem/pw14
      comparisons in all_scores.log, which are n=27 fold-0 only.

[15] statistics   VERDICT: REFUTED
      CLAIM: Per-tempo tercile conclusions on fold 0, e.g. "gated is at or below ungated on the
      slowest third every time (-0.007, -0.006, -0.042)", "gated loses on the slowest third (-0.027)
      and the fastest third (-0.022)", "no tempo group moves more than 0.007".
      CORRECTION: NOT ONE of the session's per-tempo tercile conclusions exceeds its detection
      threshold. The largest cited tercile gap, -0.042, sits at or below the 0.042-0.066 MDE for the
      slow tercile; -0.027, -0.022, -0.007, -0.006, +0.005 are all far inside it. The session's own
      remark that "a tempo group moves by 0.04 when a single track's F changes by 0.36" is right and
      should have ended the analysis. No per-tempo tercile conclusion in this session is
      statistically supportable at n=9.

[16] statistics   VERDICT: CONFIRMED
      CLAIM: Detectable effect size on F with 27 evaluation tracks; power of the paired test.
      CORRECTION: The session was chasing 0.010-0.020 F. At n=27 with the BEST-case pairing (arms
      sharing an initialisation) power at delta=0.010 is 39% — a coin flip that loses. Anything
      below ~0.017 F is undetectable on 27 tracks. And this ignores seed variance entirely: with one
      seed per arm, the config-level comparison has n=1 regardless of how many tracks are scored.
      For 80% power at delta=0.010 you need either the full 217 tracks (MDE 0.0057 at sd_d=0.030) or
      multiple seeds per arm.

[17] drift   VERDICT: CONFIRMED
      CLAIM: R4 warm-start decay attributed to corpus tempo mismatch: "The fine-tuning corpus sits
      21 BPM faster than SMC and has only half its share of slow tracks... So the warm-start decay
      you remember isn't the optimizer forgetting; it's the data pulling the model's preferred
      metrical level upward" (atext.txt:9906), restated as an action item at 9928 ("The cause is the
      corpus tempo mismatch above — 92.7 vs 71.4 BPM median... resample the fine-tuning corpus").
      CORRECTION: The 0.028 first-epoch drop is not attributable to corpus tempo mismatch. Domain
      forgetting (the fine-tuning corpus contained zero SMC tracks) is at least as good an
      explanation and was never ruled out. Neither cause is established; the correct statement is
      that the mechanism is unidentified, and the proposed tempo-resampling fix was not licensed.

[18] drift   VERDICT: CONFIRMED
      CLAIM: "The gate is done. 0 of 10 matched epochs ahead, mean −0.0157, and the deficit doesn't
      shrink with training... I'd stop gph13 and free GPU 2." (atext.txt:11480)
      CORRECTION: Both the original 'dead' and the reversal were over-read from aggregate means. The
      evidence supports: the gate is net-negative in aggregate F, and its aggregate hides a slow-
      track gain (+0.030) cancelled by fast-track damage concentrated in one 143 BPM track out of
      nine. The kill decision was right; the reasoning that produced it (aggregate mean alone) was
      not, and the reversal was driven by a 9-track-per-bin split that cannot resolve the effect.

[19] drift   VERDICT: PARTIAL
      CLAIM: "peritem is ahead in all three tempo groups at epoch 24, +0.0166 overall. That's the
      first time any arm has beaten ph13 across the board today." (atext.txt:12117), repeated in the
      ranking at 12130 as "Currently ahead".
      CORRECTION: peritem is a wash on F (mean −0.0080, scatter twice the mean), not an arm that
      beat ph13. The +0.0166 headline should never have been the lead; the running mean existed and
      was not computed until challenged.

====================================================================================================
PART 3 — LOSS SPECIFICATION
====================================================================================================

--- DESIGN_RATIONALE ---
  The spec is built on the one thing that survived every challenge: the geometry of the stock loss,
  which is fully determined by tau, pos_weight, and the max-pool, and which I re-derived by running
  the code rather than reading it. The cost accounting 7N / 16N / 39N is the load-bearing argument
  for the phase term and it checks out exactly (39 = 32 + 7), but it also exposes a coupling nobody
  stated: gamma = pos_weight/14 - 1, so gamma=1.3 is a fact about pos_weight=32, not a universal. I
  kept the phase term on mechanism and named its empirical support as weak, because the statistics
  findings rule out every fold-0 comparison that was supposed to justify it. I kept the tempo-
  relative collar only with the 2*tau floor -- the shipped min_half=2 is a live bug that penalises
  correct peaks above 76 bpm, measured on the gradient at 1204 configurations -- and I flagged it
  speculative because its one arm is confounded twice over. I refused the halving boost as shipped
  because it is arithmetically incompatible with the gamma it would ship next to. Two docstring
  numbers are simply wrong (k=0.30, sigma half-height 0.12) and I corrected both by execution. The
  invariants are written so that a test file can assert them directly, including the two process
  invariants (gamma/pos_weight coupling, evaluation power) that would have caught most of the
  session's errors.

--- EQUATIONS ---
  ALL EQUATIONS VERIFIED AGAINST THE CODE AT /home/sogang/jaehoon/Analyze-SMC/third-
  party/beat_this/beat_this/model/loss.py (mtime 2026-08-26 19:00, uncommitted) AND BY EXECUTION
  (scripts in the session scratchpad: v.py, v2.py, v3.py, v4.py).

  SYMBOLS (shared by all three forms)
  t frame index, 0..T-1, frame rate 50 fps (1 frame = 20 ms)
  z_t model output LOGIT for frame t (beat head; the downbeat head is identical with its own
  pos_weight)
  y_t binary target, 1 at an annotated beat frame, else 0
  m_t mask, 0 for padded frames and (downbeat head) for tracks with no downbeat annotation
  tau tolerance in frames, shipped value 3 (= +/-60 ms, mirrors mir_eval's +/-70 ms)
  P_tau(x)_t = max_{|d|<=tau} x_{t+d} (F.max_pool1d, kernel 2*tau+1, stride 1)
  w pos_weight (scalar in stock; 32 beat / 112 downbeat on our corpus, 20/86 in the release)
  sigma(.) logistic function
  BCE_w(z,y) = -[ w*y*log sigma(z) + (1-y)*log(1-sigma(z)) ]
  A_i frame of the i-th annotated beat; IBI_i = A_{i+1} - A_i (frames)
  phi_t phase of frame t in its enclosing annotated interval, (t - A_i)/IBI_i in [0,1), NaN outside
  [A_0, A_last]
  d(phi,psi) = min(|phi-psi|, 1-|phi-psi|) (circular distance on the phase ring)
  Valid frame set V = frames surviving the 2*tau crop at both ends (edges get no gradient).

  --------------------------------------------------------------------
  1. STOCK BEAT THIS LOSS (class ShiftTolerantBCELoss, lines 38-92)

  L_stock = (1/|V|) * sum_{t in V} u_t * BCE_w( P_tau(z)_t , y_t )

  with the "look at" weight
  u_t = y_t + (1 - P_{2tau}(y)_t) * m_t [code: look_at = targets + (1 - spread(targets,2)); look_at
  *= mask]

  Read: predictions are max-pooled by +/-tau, so a positive label's gradient goes to the LARGEST
  logit within +/-tau of it (shift tolerance). Negative supervision is switched OFF inside +/-2tau
  of any beat (the "collar" / don't-care region), because a peak placed anywhere in +/-tau is spread
  by the pooling to +/-2tau. Everything else is an ordinary weighted BCE. NOTE: the denominator is
  |V| (F.binary_cross_entropy_with_logits default reduction 'mean' divides by element count, NOT by
  sum of weights), so the weights are relative, not a weighted average.

  Structural fact (CONFIRMED, and re-derived here): a correct peak sitting at A+off with |off|<=tau
  reaches frames [A+off-tau, A+off+tau]; the union over all admissible off is [A-2tau, A+2tau].
  Hence any collar half-width < 2tau leaves part of a CORRECT peak exposed to the negative term.
  Measured: with half-width 2 and tau=3, dL/dz at a correct confident peak is POSITIVE (loss pushes
  it down) at 76, 80, 100, 120, 140, 180, 200 bpm; at half-width 6 it is negative (pushes up) at
  every bpm 30..240, every off in -3..3, every logit in {2,4,8,12}. Zero violations in 7*4*43 = 1204
  configurations.

  --------------------------------------------------------------------
  2. PHASE-WEIGHTED TERM (class PhaseWeightedShiftTolerantBCELoss, lines 369-476; arm ph13,
  gamma=1.3, sigma=0.06)

  c_t = 1 + gamma * exp( - d(phi_t, 1/2)^2 / (2 sigma^2) ), c_t := 1 where phi_t is NaN

  L_phase = (1/|V|) * sum_{t in V} u_t * [ y_t + (1-y_t) * c_t ] * BCE_w( P_tau(z)_t , y_t )

  i.e. exactly L_stock with the NEGATIVE-side weight multiplied by c_t; positives keep weight 1 so
  the miss/false-alarm exchange rate (pos_weight) is untouched. Verified by execution: with gamma=0
  the class is bit-identical to ShiftTolerantBCELoss (torch.allclose True).

  WHY PHASE COORDINATES. Every other quantity in the stock loss is in absolute frames: the collar is
  +/-2tau = +/-120 ms at all tempi, which is 8% of an IBI at 40 bpm and 36% at 180 bpm, so the
  geometry of the objective is tempo-dependent while one scalar w must serve all tempi. phi is
  tempo-invariant by construction: phi=1/2 is the subdivision midpoint whether the IBI is 1500 ms or
  333 ms. The failure being priced (double-tempo tracking) is defined as "extra peaks at the
  subdivision", which is a statement about phase, not about milliseconds. Measured behaviour of the
  shipped weight: max c = 2.2297 at phi=0.480 for IBI=25 fr, 2.2920 at phi=0.493 for IBI=75 fr (<
  1+gamma = 2.3 only because frames are discrete and no frame lands exactly on 0.5); min c = 1.0
  everywhere; the bump's >1.01 support is phi in [0.313, 0.687], which for IBI>=32 fr (<94 bpm)
  never reaches the +/-2tau collar, and above 94 bpm it does overlap the collar but has no effect
  there because u_t=0 kills the negative term inside the collar regardless of c_t.

  --------------------------------------------------------------------
  3. PROPOSED FINAL LOSS

  L_final = (1/|V|) * sum_{t in V} U_t * [ y_t + (1-y_t) * c_t ] * BCE_w( P_tau(z)_t , y_t )

  U_t = y_t + (1 - C_t) * m_t, C_t = P_{H}(y)_t (per-item, padded max-pool, length preserved)
  H = clip( round(k * median_i IBI_i), H_min, H_max ), H_min = 2*tau, H_max = 40, k = 0.14
  c_t as in section 2, gamma = 1.3, sigma = 0.06.

  Two departures from the shipped TempoRelativeCollarBCELoss, both forced by measurement:
  (a) H_min = 2*tau = 6, NOT the shipped default 2. At min_half=2 the loss penalises correct peaks
  above ~76 bpm (measured above).
  (b) Consequence to state plainly: with k=0.14 and H_min=6, H = 6 for every IBI <= 46 fr (>= 65
  bpm), so the term is a pure WIDENING of the collar below 65 bpm and a no-op above it. The
  docstring's "narrows 180 bpm to ~5" is unreachable once the floor is sound. The collar term is
  therefore only a slow-tempo intervention.

  TERM STATUS:
  - Shift-tolerant BCE core: KEEP. It is the verified baseline.
  - Phase suppression c_t (gamma=1.3, sigma=0.06): KEEP as the primary term, but its empirical
  support is WEAK, not established. ph13's fold-0 0.6568 vs released 0.6510 is n=27 fold-0 only,
  differs in >=4 variables (loss, pos_weight 32/112 vs 20/86, corpus composition, training code),
  and sits far inside the real noise floor (sd of a single-seed fold-0 F ~ 0.031; MDE at n=27 with
  best-case pairing ~0.017 F). The term is retained on MECHANISM (the cost-parity argument, which is
  arithmetically sound, and the tempo-invariance argument), not on a measured win. Say so in any
  write-up.
  - Tempo-relative collar with floor 2*tau: SPECULATIVE. The only arm that tested it (collar14) is
  confounded in two variables at once (relative collar AND absence of the phase term), so its -0.014
  attributes to neither; and collar14 is the sole phase5 arm on the post-19:00 loss.py, whose diff
  is unrecoverable. Include it only behind a flag, default OFF, until a one-variable arm exists.
  - Halving boost h_i: SPECULATIVE and, as calibrated, arithmetically incompatible with gamma=1.3
  (see rejected/constants). Do NOT ship it together with gamma=1.3 unchanged.

  If the halving boost were added, the only coherent form is:
  h_i = a_{i-1} * a_{i+1} * (1 - a_i), a_i = sigma(P_tau(z)_{A_i}) (activation at the i-th annotated
  beat)
  positive-side weight y_t -> y_t * (1 + gamma_h * h_{i(t)})
  and gamma must be RE-DERIVED jointly (section 4), not left at 1.3.

  DEGENERATE-CASE CHECK (executed): with gamma=0 and H forced to 6, L_final is torch.allclose to
  L_stock. The proposal is a strict superset of the baseline.

--- CONSTANTS ---
  EVERY CONSTANT, ITS VALUE, AND ITS DERIVATION. "MEASURED" = I ran it this session; "INHERITED" = a
  session number I could not re-measure from an artifact.

  tau = 3 frames (+/-60 ms at 50 fps)
  Derivation: mirrors mir_eval's fixed +/-70 ms hit window. Deliberately NOT made tempo-relative: a
  relative tolerance at 40 bpm would be +/-150 ms, training would call "close enough" what the
  metric scores as a miss. Rule: normalise what the metric does not constrain, leave aligned what it
  does.

  collar half-width (stock) = 2*tau = 6 frames (13 frames total, +/-120 ms)
  Derivation MEASURED: a correct peak at A+off, |off|<=tau, is max-pooled to [A+off-tau, A+off+tau];
  union over |off|<=tau is [A-2tau, A+2tau]. So 2*tau is the STRUCTURAL MINIMUM, not a taste
  parameter.

  w (pos_weight) = 32 beat / 112 downbeat on our corpus (release: 20 / 86)
  Derivation: w = (total_frames - beats*(2*tau+1)) / beats over the unaugmented training tracks.
  w=32 implies ~39 frames per beat = 0.78 s = ~77 bpm, i.e. the objective carries an implicit
  preferred beat rate. CONFIRMED at launch. NOTE the hand-calc that said 30 was wrong; 32 is the
  launched value.

  gamma = 1.3 (phase suppression strength)
  Derivation MEASURED (cost parity, per N annotated beats, at tau=3, w=32):
  doubling : all N beats hit, N spurious peaks. One confident spurious peak drives 2*tau+1 = 7
  negative frames -> cost 7N.
  halving : N/2 beats missed, each at positive weight w -> cost (N/2)*w = 16N.
  offbeat : all N missed (wN = 32N) plus N spurious (7N) -> 39N.
  So under the stock loss the coherent wrong metrical level is the CHEAPEST error available. Parity:
  7N(1+gamma) = 16N -> gamma = 16/7 - 1 = 1.2857 -> 1.3. VERIFIED arithmetically; the 7N/16N/39N
  accounting is internally consistent (39 = 32 + 7 exactly).
  CRITICAL CAVEAT, newly derived here: gamma is a function of w, not a universal constant.
  gamma*(w, tau) = w / (2*(2*tau+1)) - 1 = w/14 - 1 at tau=3.
  w=32 -> 1.286; w=20 (the release) -> 0.429; w=14 (arm pw14) -> 0.0.
  Any change to pos_weight invalidates gamma=1.3. At w=14 the parity gamma is exactly zero, i.e. the
  phase term is unmotivated at that pos_weight. This coupling was not stated in the session and must
  be in the spec.

  sigma = 0.06 (phase bump width, in IBI units)
  Derivation MEASURED: half-height at d = sigma*sqrt(2 ln 2) = 0.06*1.17741 = 0.07064 IBI, i.e.
  +/-0.0706, NOT the +/-0.12 the docstring claims (overstated by 1.67x). The docstring is wrong; the
  code is fine. Practical support (c > 1.01) is phi in [0.313, 0.687], half-extent 0.1872 IBI.
  Constraint sigma must satisfy: the bump must not reach the beat itself. Beat frames sit at phase
  distance 0.5 from the bump centre, and the collar occupies |phi| <= 2*tau/IBI. Non-interference
  requires 0.5 - sigma*sqrt(2 ln(gamma/eps)) > 2*tau/IBI_min. At sigma=0.06 this holds down to IBI =
  32 frames (94 bpm); above 94 bpm the supports overlap but the effect is nil because u_t = 0 inside
  the collar. MEASURED.

  k = 0.14 (tempo-relative collar fraction)
  Derivation MEASURED: k*IBI(70 bpm) = 0.14*42.9 = 6.0 -> half 6 -> 13 frames total = exactly the
  stock collar. So k=0.14 is the value that pins 70 bpm to the stock behaviour. The docstring's "k =
  0.30 leaves 70 bpm unchanged (13 frames)" is REFUTED by execution: k=0.30 at 70 bpm gives half 13,
  27 frames total. The docstring's worked example both uses a k the code does not ship and mislabels
  half-widths as totals.
  Measured k=0.14 table (frames, half / total): 40 bpm 11/23; 70 bpm 6/13; 120 bpm 4/9; 180 bpm 2/5
  -- the last two are BELOW the structural floor and are clamped up to 6 by H_min.

  H_min = 2*tau = 6 (NOT the shipped default 2)
  Derivation MEASURED: at H_min=2, dL/dz at a correctly placed confident peak is positive (loss
  pushes it down) at 76, 80, 100, 120, 140, 180, 200 bpm; the affected offsets widen with tempo
  (+/-3 at 76 bpm, all of -3..+3 at 180 bpm) and the defect appears once the logit exceeds ~3 (at
  logit 2 the peak is still pushed up; at logit 4, 8, 12 it is pushed down). At H_min=6: zero
  violations across 43 tempi x 7 offsets x 4 logits = 1204 cases.

  H_max = 40 frames
  Purely a guard against a degenerate median IBI on a near-empty annotation. No derivation;
  arbitrary. Flag it as such.

  gamma_h ~ 0.295 (halving boost) -- RE-DERIVED, and the session's number is right but its use is
  not
  INHERITED input: mean h at missed beats on halved tracks = 0.3385 (session measurement; I could
  not re-measure it, so treat as UNVERIFIED-by-me).
  "10% parity" means the boost should raise the halving cost by 10%: gamma_h * 0.3385 = 0.10 ->
  gamma_h = 0.2954 -> ~0.30. The session's 0.30 is arithmetically correct.
  BUT the joint calibration is then inconsistent. With the boost active, halving costs 16N*(1 +
  0.3385*gamma_h) = 17.6N while doubling still costs 7N*(1+gamma) = 16N at gamma=1.3. Parity
  requires
  gamma = (16/7)*(1 + 0.3385*gamma_h) - 1 = 1.514 at gamma_h = 0.2954.
  So gamma=1.3 AND gamma_h=0.30 shipped together make halving 10% dearer than doubling -- a
  deliberate over-correction of the exact error the phase term already fixed, in the opposite
  direction. Either ship gamma=1.3 with gamma_h=0, or ship the pair (gamma=1.514, gamma_h=0.295). Do
  not mix.

  ref frames/beat = 39, min_w = 2, max_w = 128 (DensityWeighted), phase_gamma default 1.3 /
  phase_sigma default 0.06 in code: recorded for completeness; the density arm is ruled out (see
  rejected).

--- REJECTED ---
  WHAT THE VERIFIED EVIDENCE RULES OUT, WITH THE MEASURED REASON.

  1. PER-ITEM pos_weight (PerItemShiftTolerantBCELoss, w_i = (valid_i - beats_i*(2tau+1))/beats_i)
  RULED OUT. The sign is backwards. It gives a 40 bpm excerpt ~68 and a 180 bpm excerpt ~10, i.e. it
  raises the pressure on exactly the excerpts already over-firing, and made doubling WORSE (0.511 ->
  0.578 on the doubling rate, per the shipped docstring's own record). Independently, both phase4
  peritem arms trained on the 1954-track corpus with zero SMC, so their fold-0 numbers cannot
  baseline anything on the 2678-track corpus. And the "+0.0166 at epoch 24, ahead in all three tempo
  groups" claim was a wash on the running mean (-0.0080, scatter twice the mean) once it was
  actually computed.

  2. GLOBAL pos_weight REDUCTION (arm pw14, beat=14)
  RULED OUT as a substitute for the phase term, on arithmetic that is now explicit: the cost-parity
  gamma is w/14 - 1 at tau=3, so w=14 sets the doubling/halving parity gamma to exactly 0. Lowering
  w to 14 makes halving as cheap as doubling by construction rather than making doubling expensive;
  it removes the asymmetry instead of correcting it, and it moves the implicit preferred beat rate
  rather than deleting it. Separately, pw14 is the ONE arm where the "all arms ran at pos_weight 32"
  claim is false, so it is not comparable to the rest of the sweep on any other axis either.

  3. THE CONFIDENCE GATE (GatedPhaseShiftTolerantBCELoss, gph13)
  RULED OUT. 0 of 10 matched epochs ahead of ungated ph13, mean -0.0157, and the deficit did not
  shrink with training. The kill decision stands. Two honesty notes that must travel with it: (a)
  the decision was made on an aggregate mean alone, which was not sufficient reasoning even though
  the conclusion held; (b) the later "reversal" -- that the gate wins on slow tracks (+0.030) and
  loses on fast ones -- rests on a 9-track-per-bin split whose MDE is 0.042-0.066, so it cannot
  resolve an effect of that size and must not be reported as a finding. The gate is out; the tempo
  story about it is unsupported.

  4. sigma >= 0.15 for the phase bump
  RULED OUT on geometry, measured: at sigma=0.15 the half-height is 0.15*1.17741 = 0.1766 IBI and
  the >1.01 support extends to +/-0.468 IBI, which reaches phase 0.032 -- essentially the beat
  itself. At any tempo the bump would then be pressing down the region the collar exists to protect,
  and above ~94 bpm it overlaps the collar outright. sigma must stay small enough that 0.5 -
  sigma*sqrt(2 ln(gamma/eps)) > 2*tau/IBI_min. sigma=0.06 satisfies this down to IBI=32 frames;
  sigma=0.15 satisfies it for no realistic tempo.

  5. SUB-FLOOR COLLARS (any collar half-width < 2*tolerance, including the shipped min_half=2)
  RULED OUT, measured directly on the gradient. At min_half=2 the loss actively pushes DOWN a
  correctly placed, confident peak at 76 bpm and above -- the majority of any real corpus -- because
  the prediction max-pool spreads the peak to +/-2*tau while the don't-care region only covers +/-2.
  Violations appear at logit >= ~4 and widen with tempo (offsets +/-3 at 76 bpm; the entire -3..+3
  window at 180 bpm). At min_half=6 there are zero violations over 1204 tested (tempo, offset,
  logit) combinations. Corollary: the tempo-relative collar can only ever WIDEN (below ~65 bpm at
  k=0.14) once the floor is imposed; the "narrow fast tempi" half of its motivation is unreachable
  and must be dropped from the docstring.

  6. THE HALVING BOOST h_i AT gamma_h = 0.30 ALONGSIDE gamma = 1.3
  RULED OUT AS A PAIR (the boost itself is merely unproven). gamma=1.3 ALREADY reaches
  doubling/halving cost parity by construction; the 7N/16N/39N accounting is arithmetically sound
  and self-consistent (39 = 32+7 exactly at w=32, tau=3). Any gamma_h > 0 therefore pushes the
  halving cost ABOVE the doubling cost -- 17.6N vs 16.0N at gamma_h=0.295, hbar=0.3385 -- which
  over-corrects into the opposite error. If the boost is wanted, gamma must rise to 1.514 to restore
  parity. Note also that hbar=0.3385 is an inherited session measurement I did not re-measure, so
  the whole gamma_h derivation rests on an unverified input.

  7. ALL FOLD-0-ONLY EVIDENCE AS A BASIS FOR CHOOSING BETWEEN LOSSES
  RULED OUT as decisive. Every ph13 / gph13 / sig10 / bidir03 / collar14 / peritem / pw14 comparison
  in all_scores.log is n=27, one seed, one checkpoint. The standard error of a 27-track fold mean
  relative to the 217-track corpus value is 0.0446, larger than the observed between-fold sd of
  0.0320 -- fold-to-fold variation is essentially all sampling noise, and even "fold 0 is easier" is
  not established (Welch t=0.52, p=0.605). At n=27 with best-case pairing, power at delta=0.010 is
  39%; nothing below ~0.017 F is detectable. The session's 0.007 noise floor understates the real
  figure by 4-6x. Consequences for this spec: collar14's -0.014 is uninformative (and doubly so,
  being confounded in two variables plus an unrecoverable 19:00 loss.py edit); ph13's +0.0058 over
  the release is uninformative (and confounded in at least four variables, of which the release's
  actual training track list is ASSUMED, never measured); and the f0_wide/f0_shipped phase3 trio
  cannot baseline ph13 at all (1954 tracks, zero SMC, vs 2678 with 200 SMC) though the phase3 pair
  remains internally valid against each other.

  8. R4 WARM-START DECAY ATTRIBUTED TO CORPUS TEMPO MISMATCH -> the proposed tempo-resampling fix
  RULED OUT as licensed. The 0.028 first-epoch drop is equally well explained by domain forgetting
  (the fine-tuning corpus contained zero SMC tracks), which was never ruled out. The mechanism is
  unidentified; do not resample the corpus on this basis and do not let this reasoning into the loss
  design.

--- INVARIANTS ---
  1. INV1 STRUCTURAL COLLAR FLOOR: for every tempo, every offset off in [-tau, tau], and every peak
  logit in {2,4,8,12}, dL/dz at a correctly-placed peak must be <= 0 (loss pushes it UP, never
  down). Executable: build y with beats every IBI frames, z = -8 everywhere except logit L at A+off;
  assert loss(z,y).backward(); z.grad[A+off] <= 0 for IBI in round(3000/bpm) for bpm in
  range(30,241,5). MEASURED: 0/1204 violations at collar half-width 6; 4xx violations at half-width
  2 for bpm >= 76.
  2. INV2 DEGENERATE REDUCTION: with phase_gamma=0 and the collar half-width forced to 2*tolerance,
  the loss must be bit-identical to ShiftTolerantBCELoss. Executable: assert
  torch.allclose(Final(pos_weight=32, phase_gamma=0., min_half=6)(z,y),
  ShiftTolerantBCELoss(pos_weight=32)(z,y)). MEASURED True.
  3. INV3 PHASE WEIGHT RANGE: 1.0 <= c_t <= 1 + phase_gamma for every frame, and c_t == 1.0 exactly
  at every annotated beat frame and at every frame outside [A_0, A_last]. Executable: w =
  loss._phase_weight(y); assert w.min() == 1.0 and w.max() <= 1 + gamma + 1e-6 and torch.all(w[y>0]
  == 1.0). MEASURED min 1.0, max 2.2297 <= 2.3.
  4. INV4 POSITIVE SIDE UNTOUCHED BY THE PHASE TERM: the effective weight on any frame with y_t == 1
  must be independent of phase_gamma, so the miss/false-alarm exchange rate stays exactly
  pos_weight. Executable: assert the total loss contribution of the positive frames is unchanged
  when gamma is swept 0 -> 3 with z fixed.
  5. INV5 COLLAR NON-INTERFERENCE: the phase bump must never change the loss inside the don't-care
  collar. Executable: assert (look_at * (c - 1))[collar_mask].abs().max() == 0. Holds structurally
  because look_at = 0 there; must be re-asserted after any refactor that reorders the
  multiplications.
  6. INV6 GAMMA/POS_WEIGHT COUPLING: whenever pos_weight is changed, phase_gamma must be recomputed
  as pos_weight/(2*(2*tolerance+1)) - 1, or the change must be explicitly recorded as a deliberate
  departure from cost parity. Executable: assert abs(phase_gamma - (pos_weight/(2*(2*tolerance+1)) -
  1)) < 0.05 or config['parity_override'] is True. At pos_weight=14 the parity gamma is 0, i.e. the
  term is unmotivated.
  7. INV7 JOINT PARITY WITH THE HALVING BOOST: if gamma_h > 0, then phase_gamma must equal
  ((2*pos_weight/(2*(2*tolerance+1)))/2)*(1 + hbar*gamma_h) - 1, i.e. (pos_weight/14)*(1 +
  hbar*gamma_h) - 1 at tolerance=3, with hbar the measured mean gate value at missed beats.
  Executable: assert gamma_h == 0 or abs(phase_gamma - ((pos_weight/14)*(1 + hbar*gamma_h) - 1)) <
  0.05. At gamma_h=0.295, hbar=0.3385, pos_weight=32 this requires phase_gamma=1.514, not 1.3.
  8. INV8 NO GRADIENT THROUGH THE WEIGHTS: c_t, the collar mask, and any h_i gate must be computed
  under torch.no_grad or from targets only, so no gradient flows through the weighting. Executable:
  assert not c.requires_grad and not collar.requires_grad. (c is targets-only in the current code;
  an h_i gate built from activations WOULD carry gradient and must be detached explicitly.)
  9. INV9 SHAPE AND LENGTH PRESERVATION: the per-item relative collar must return a tensor of the
  same length as targets (padded max-pool), so the existing crop/spread arithmetic is unchanged.
  Executable: assert loss._relative_collar(y).shape == y.shape for random beat layouts including
  len(pos) in {0,1,2}.
  10. INV10 ONE-COLUMN / MISSING-ANNOTATION SAFETY: items with fewer than 2 annotated beats must
  fall back to the fixed 2*tau collar and c_t == 1 everywhere, never produce NaN, and never be
  silently mis-supervised. Executable: assert torch.isfinite(loss(z, y_empty)) and
  torch.isfinite(loss(z, y_single)). (The dataloader previously SKIPPED one-column tracks entirely
  -- CONFIRMED -- so any change that starts admitting them must satisfy this.)
  11. INV11 EVALUATION POWER GUARD (process invariant, not code): no configuration decision may be
  taken from a single-seed fold-0 comparison. sd of a single-seed single-checkpoint fold-0 F is
  ~0.031 (seed sd 0.028 over 3 seeds, checkpoint sd ~0.013); the sd of a two-arm one-seed difference
  is ~0.044 at n=1 pair. Executable as a check on the reporting script: assert (n_tracks >= 217 and
  observed_delta >= 0.0057) or n_seeds >= 3, else label the result UNDERPOWERED. Every 0.007-noise-
  floor judgement in the session violated this.

  1.110e-15 -> IMPLEMENTATION FIXED (test not weakened). The inherited Gaussian is untruncated, so c

  the bump is zeroed beyond 4*sigma = 0.24 IBI. Largest discarded value gamma*exp(-8) = 4.4e-4; the

  <= gamma (1.3) instead of c <= 1+gamma (2.3). The measured max 2.3000 is correct and is reached
  exactly at 100 bpm (IBI=30, a frame lands exactly on phi=0.5). Bound corrected to 2.3. FAIL phase-
  term pressure increase stays under 25% at every tempo max delta +49.5346% -> MY THRESHOLD WAS
  INVENTED, not derived from the spec or the geometry. The real value is up to +49.53% at 180 bpm.
  Replaced with the only bound the geometry implies (delta <= gamma = 130%, since every negative
  weight lies in [1, 1+gamma]), and the tempo profile is now printed in full plus asserted to be
  non-flat, so the confound is reported rather than asserted away. Also fixed during bring-up: the

  "Index put requires the source and destination dtypes match, got Double for the destination and
  Float for the source" on float64 targets (and silently down-casts otherwise). Overridden dtype-
  correctly in the new class; the existing class was not modified.

--- notes ---
  IMPLEMENTATION - New class FinalPhaseCollarBCELoss appended to loss.py; pure addition (git diff
  shows 0 deleted lines in loss.py). No existing class or arm modified. - Registered as loss_type
  "final_phase_collar_bce" in beat_this/model/pl_module.py and launch_scripts/train.py, with new
  flags --final-relative-collar, --final-halving-gamma, --parity-override. Defaults:
  phase_gamma=1.3, phase_sigma=0.06, relative_collar=False, halving_gamma=0.0,
  min_half=2*tolerance=6 (constructor REFUSES anything smaller), max_half=40. Downbeat head stays on
  stock ShiftTolerantBCELoss because the parity gamma is a function of pos_weight (w/14 - 1), so 1.3
  is a fact about the beat head's 32, not the downbeat's 112. - pl_module calls check_parity() at
  construction: PLBeatThis(pos_weights={'beat':14,...}, loss_type='final_phase_collar_bce') raises.
  Verified by execution. TWO DEPARTURES FROM THE SPEC AS WRITTEN 1. phase_cut=4.0 truncation added
  so the penalty is EXACTLY zero at phi=0 (the spec demands zero mass on annotated beats; the
  untruncated form leaves 8e-16). 2. _phase overridden for dtype correctness (inherited float32
  bug). MEASURED NUMBERS - Reduction to stock: max |final - stock| = 0.0 exactly, both with collar
  off and with relative_collar=True/k=0, over 40/55/70/100/143/180 bpm, batch 3, with padding and
  fully-masked items. - No-downward-push: 0/168 violations per collar mode (6 tempi x 7 offsets x 4
  logits). Adversarial control with min_half forced to 2: 17/42 violations, at 100/143/180 bpm -
  confirms the test has teeth and the 2*tau floor is what prevents the collar14 defect. -
  Detachment: gate/phase/collar all grad_fn None; dL/dz bit-identical (max diff 0.0) to a gate-
  frozen reference. - NEGATIVE PRESSURE vs stock (sum of negative-side weights), phase term only:
  40bpm +22.76%, 55 +24.20%, 70 +25.92%, 100 +30.18%, 143 +39.30%, 180 +49.53%. Tempo skew +26.8%
  between 40 and 180 bpm. With the relative collar also on: 40bpm +6.56%, 55 +14.81%, identical to
  phase-only at >=70 bpm. THIS IS A REAL CONFOUND inherent to the spec's un-normalised L_final:
  extra negative pressure alone produces halving, and here it is tempo-dependent, so any tempo-split
  reading of a phase-term arm is confounded unless the arm normalises or the confound is measured
  out. Printed prominently by the test. - Relative collar is a bit-exact no-op at >=70 bpm (floor
  binds at k=0.14), confirming the spec's statement that it is a slow-tempo widening only and cannot
  "narrow 180 bpm to ~5". Per-beat collar frames at 40/100/180 bpm = 23/13/13. - Phase weight range
  over 40-180 bpm: [1.0000, 2.3000]; 2.3000 is hit exactly at 100 bpm where a frame lands on
  phi=0.5. c == 1.0 exactly at every beat and everywhere outside [A_0, A_last]. - Positive-side
  contribution invariant under gamma sweep 0 -> 1.3 -> 3: identical to 0.0. - Degenerate (0, 1, 2,
  adjacent IBI=1, all-frames beats): finite loss and grad in both collar modes. - Mixed batch: per-
  item collar and phase weights differ; batched loss == mean of per-item losses to <1e-10. - Mask:
  perturbing masked frames by +17 logits changes the loss by exactly 0.0; fully masked item gets
  exactly zero gradient. Both collar modes. - Parity: parity_gamma = w/14 - 1 verified at w=32
  (1.2857), 20 (0.4286), 14 (0.0). gamma=1.3 refused at w=14; joint parity with gamma_h=0.295,
  hbar=0.3385 requires gamma=1.514, so 1.3 is refused there too. UNVERIFIED - hbar = 0.3385 (mean
  gate value at missed beats) is an inherited session measurement I did not re-measure; the joint-
  parity constant 1.514 rests on it. - H_max = 40 has no derivation; it is an arbitrary guard,
  flagged as such in the docstring. - No training was launched, touched, or inspected. All work CPU-
  only.

--- blockers_remaining ---
  Both stated blockers are reproduced in the script header and remain unresolved: 1.
  TempoRelativeCollarBCELoss docstring describes the collar as a pure tempo-normalisation of the
  stock "don't care" region, with nothing about correct peaks being penalised; code default
  min_half=2 (verified in the signature, and note 2 != 2*tolerance = 6). The "collar narrower than
  2*tolerance penalises correct peaks" justification appears only in the final_phase_collar_bce
  comment in pl_module.py, not in the collar class's own docstring. This is why final_s0 runs with
  --final-relative-collar OFF. 2. Detectable effect size on F with 27 evaluation tracks and the
  power of the paired test have NOT been computed. Against a measured stock seed spread of 0.056 in
  F, the minimum resolvable difference for this design is UNVERIFIED. Additional unverified item: I
  could not recover the exact original launch command for phase5/ph13 from the transcript with its
  --checkpoint-dir intact, only the flag pattern (--loss phase_shift_tolerant_weighted_bce --phase-
  gamma 1.3 --data-dir /disk1/jaehoon/bt_wide/data). ph13_s1 matches that pattern (--phase-sigma
  0.06 is the default, so stating it explicitly is value-identical), but that the existing ph13 run
  used no other non-default flag is UNVERIFIED.
